security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU emulates the IOPMP register map using the pre-v0.8.1 layout (HWCFG0 fields at wrong bit positions, ENTRYOFFSET at 0x14 instead of 0x2C, no HWCFG2/HWCFG3 registers) while the guest kernel is compiled against spec v0.8.1, OR QEMU incorrectly reports HWCFG0.HWCFG2_en/HWCFG3_en as 0 when HWCFG2/HWCFG3 fields are implemented (or 1 when they are not), OR QEMU fails to implement write-1-clear sticky-bit semantics on HWCFG2.prio_ent_prog and HWCFG3.rrid_transl_prog, allowing a malicious guest to reprogram locked priority-entry count or RRID translation after IOPMP enforcement has been configured.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: hwcfg[023] bitfield layout mismatch with spec v0.8.1; ENTRYOFFSET register offset hardcoded to 0x14; HWCFG2_en / HWCFG3_en not conditionally exposed; write-1-clear sticky bits implemented as plain r/w; prio_ent_prog / rrid_transl_prog writable after lock; non_prio_en ignored when computing priority-entry range; hwcfg2_t / hwcfg3_t struct bit positions diverged from spec
security_spec.summary: IOPMP spec v0.8.1 reorganizes bit fields across HWCFG0/HWCFG2/HWCFG3 with conditional register presence and write-1-clear sticky bits; incorrect QEMU emulation of this register-remap allows a malicious guest VM to bypass IOPMP DMA access controls, enabling privilege escape from the guest to other guests or the host via misconfigured IO memory protection

location.file_path: N/A - QEMU has no IOPMP source files

findings.finding: QEMU does not implement any IOPMP device model. There is no IOPMP register map, no HWCFG0/HWCFG1/HWCFG2/HWCFG3 registers, no ENTRYOFFSET register, no write-1-clear sticky-bit logic, and no priority/non-priority entry enforcement. The entire IOPMP subsystem is absent from the QEMU codebase. A comprehensive grep for 'iopmp', 'IOPMP', 'ENTRYOFFSET', 'prio_ent_prog', 'rrid_transl_prog', 'non_prio_en', 'hwcfg2_t', 'hwcfg3_t' across the entire repository returned zero relevant results. The only HWCFG-like matches are in the unrelated Synopsys DWC2 USB controller (hw/usb/dwc2-regs.h).
findings.snippet: No IOPMP code exists in QEMU to cite.

findings.finding: False positive: The USB DWC2 controller defines macros with substring 'HWCFG' (GHWCFG1, GHWCFG2, GHWCFG3, GHWCFG4). These are Synopsys DesignWare USB 2.0 hardware configuration registers, completely unrelated to RISC-V IOPMP. No security concern.
findings.snippet: USB DWC2 HWCFG macros are unrelated to IOPMP.

findings.finding: The IOPMP reference model (NOT QEMU code) correctly implements spec v0.8.2: HWCFG2 at offset 0x10, HWCFG3 at offset 0x14, ENTRYOFFSET at offset 0x2C. HWCFG2.prio_ent_prog uses write-1-clear (&= ~hwcfg2_temp.prio_ent_prog at line 584). HWCFG3.rrid_transl_prog uses write-1-clear (&= ~hwcfg3_temp.rrid_transl_prog at line 600). prio_entry writable only when prio_ent_prog=1 (line 581-583). rrid_transl writable only when rrid_transl_prog=1 (line 597-599). md_entry_num locked when HWCFG0.enable=1 (line 592-595). HWCFG0.HWCFG2_en and HWCFG0.HWCFG3_en are hardcoded to 1 (lines 127-128). These implementations match the spec exactly.
